indicators._note: Stalkerware: Echap/stalkerware-indicators (github.com/Te-k/stalkerware-indicators, ioc.yaml, fetched 2026-10-22) — 614 packages and 473 signing-cert SHA-1 fingerprints across 132 families; an app matches on package OR cert, so a renamed sample signed with the same key is still caught. Mercenary: Android app ids from MVT (mvt-project/mvt-indicators) RCS Lab Hermit, WyrmSpy/DragonEgg, Spyrtacus, Morpheus, ResidentBat and Cellebrite sets. Allow-lists (screen_readers/parental_control/known_good_keyboards) match by package and are honoured only for a system or store-installed app, or when a cert_sha1 is pinned (review N2), so a sideloaded impostor cannot borrow the name.

rules.title: Known stalkerware app
rules.explain: This app matches a known stalkerware product by its package or signing certificate. Apps like this are sold to monitor another person's phone.

rules.title: Known mercenary-spyware indicator
rules.explain: This app matches a published indicator for mercenary spyware (for example from Amnesty International or Citizen Lab).

rules.title: Someone opened your canary link
rules.explain: A private link placed in your own notes was opened from a device that is not yours, which means someone is reading your messages.

rules.title: Hidden sideloaded app that can read your screen
rules.explain: This app can read everything on your screen and what you type, it was installed from outside an app store, and it hides its icon. Legitimate apps rarely do all three.

rules.title: App that uploads while your screen is off
rules.explain: This app can read your screen and sent data out while your screen was off, a pattern typical of monitoring apps.

rules.title: Sideloaded app holding several surveillance powers
rules.explain: This app was installed from outside an app store and holds two or more of the powers stalkerware needs (reading your screen, notifications, texts or being a device administrator).

rules.title: Hidden app holding a surveillance power
rules.explain: This app keeps no icon in your app list, holds a power that can watch you, and was installed from outside an app store. Hiding the icon is a common stalkerware trait.

rules.title: App's signing certificate changed on update
rules.explain: This app was replaced by a version signed by someone different from before. That is how a trusted app can be swapped for a repackaged, tampered one.

rules.title: Sideloaded app with a surveillance power
rules.explain: This app was installed from outside an app store and holds a power that could be used to watch you. Worth a look if you did not install it yourself.

rules.title: App can read your screen (accessibility)
rules.explain: This app has accessibility access, which lets it read your screen and what you type. Many legitimate tools use it too, so check whether you recognise this one.

rules.title: App's install source looks faked
rules.explain: This app claims to come from an app store, but the record of who installed it does not line up. Someone with physical access can fake the store label when sideloading.

rules.title: Parental-control app on your own phone
rules.explain: This is a known parental-control product. On a child's phone that is expected, but on your own phone an app that can monitor and restrict you is worth a careful look — stalkerware is often sold as parental control.

rules.title: Unrecognised keyboard app
rules.explain: A keyboard app can see everything you type. This one is not a recognised mainstream keyboard, so it is worth a look if you did not install it yourself.

rules.title: Hidden app holding a surveillance power
rules.explain: This app keeps no icon in your app list yet holds a power that can watch you. Many legitimate components (a watch companion, a system helper) do this too, so check whether you recognise it.

rules.title: Screen reader you turned on
rules.explain: This app is a recognised screen reader, an assistive tool. Its accessibility access, and its having no icon in the app list, are explained by that.

rules.title: Parental-control product
rules.explain: This app is a known parental-control product, which explains its accessibility access. It is still shown as worth a look because on your own phone such an app can be misused to monitor you.
